name: Klebanov-Witten Conifold Throat
description: The throat of threebranes at a conifold singularity: anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times the compact space $T^{1,1}$. Its internal circle twists over two 2-spheres, and a self-dual five-form flux supports the curvature of the ten dimensions.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit and use the Ricci contraction $R_{\mu\nu}=R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: The compact dimensions of the Klebanov-Witten throat form a circle bundle over two 2-spheres. Igor R. Klebanov and Edward Witten identified the throat of threebranes at a conifold singularity with anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions times $T^{1,1}$ in 1998 [klebanovwitten1998]. The anti-de Sitter factor contains time and four spatial dimensions. The remaining five dimensions form the compact space $T^{1,1}$.¶Philip Candelas and Xenia C. de la Ossa constructed the conifold's Ricci flat Kähler metric in 1990 [candelas1990conifold, klebanovwitten1998]. It is a cone over $T^{1,1}$, whose angular distances grow in proportion to the distance from its tip. The cone has six spatial dimensions and supplies the geometry transverse to the threebranes. Its tip is a curvature singularity, where the compact base shrinks to a point.¶Larry James Romans had included this compactification among his solutions of chiral supergravity in 1985 [romans1985compactification]. The internal space is the quotient $(SU(2)\times SU(2))/U(1)$, with the circle embedded diagonally in the two factors. Its isometries form $SU(2)\times SU(2)\times U(1)$, and the compactification preserves eight supersymmetries [klebanovwitten1998].¶Klebanov and Witten proposed that string theory on this throat is dual to a conformal gauge theory in four dimensions [klebanovwitten1998]. The gauge group is $SU(N)\times SU(N)$, where $N$ counts the threebranes. Two pairs of matter fields couple the two gauge groups, and a quartic superpotential preserves the two sphere symmetries. The resulting theory has $\mathcal{N}=1$ supersymmetry, with four ordinary supersymmetries and four conformal partners.¶The two factors share one curvature scale [klebanovwitten1998]. The compact base has positive Einstein curvature, and its normalization makes the cone Ricci flat. In the throat, the five-form flux supports a nonzero Ricci tensor, with equal and opposite eigenvalues on the two factors. Its ten-dimensional scalar curvature vanishes, and its curvature remains finite at the Poincaré horizon.

related.text: Both throats arise from threebranes and pair anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions with a compact space of the same radius. A round 5-sphere preserves 32 supersymmetries, while $T^{1,1}$ preserves eight and has $SU(2)\times SU(2)\times U(1)$ isometry [klebanovwitten1998].

The noncompact factor is anti-de Sitter space of five dimensions, with the same constant negative curvature construction as the geometry of four dimensions. The compact factor is $T^{1,1}$ [klebanovwitten1998].
Both geometries contain a spatial circle fibred over a 2-sphere. The internal circle of the throat has a connection with one contribution from each of two 2-spheres [klebanovwitten1998].
The angular connection in Taub-NUT and the circle fibre of $T^{1,1}$ both twist over a 2-sphere. The throat's fibre is spatial and extends over two spheres [klebanovwitten1998].

coordinates.name: Poincaré

parameters.description: The common curvature length of the anti-de Sitter and compact factors, with $L>0$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t,x,y,z,r,\theta_1,\phi_1,\theta_2,\phi_2,\psi)$, with $t$ a time, $x$, $y$, $z$, and $r$ lengths, and the remaining coordinates dimensionless angles. The angles $(\theta_1,\phi_1)$ and $(\theta_2,\phi_2)$ parametrize the two 2-spheres, and $\psi$ parametrizes the circle fibre. We take components in the chart $x^0=ct$, with a dot denoting differentiation with respect to an affine parameter $\lambda$.
